title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel not eaten, with added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a dish made from fresh potato tubers that are cooked in water without the skin. A small amount of fat (oil or butter) is often added during cooking to improve flavor and texture. Potatoes are a major source of carbohydrates, B‑vitamins, and potassium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
Boiled potatoes without skin are easier to digest than raw potatoes.
Adding a little fat enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin A.
Cooked potatoes can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week if stored in an airtight container.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, but high‑starch types are preferred for boiling.

items.title: Rich source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Boiled potatoes retain some vitamin C, an antioxidant that protects cells.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The starch in boiled potatoes is easily broken down, providing a quick energy source.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in neurotransmitter synthesis and protein metabolism.

items.title: Low in sodium
items.content: When prepared without added salt, boiled potatoes fit low‑sodium diets.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be an issue for people with diabetes.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rare but possible allergic reactions to potato proteins.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged high‑heat cooking can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Excess fat
items.content: Adding too much fat increases calorie content and may contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled, peeled potatoes can be eaten plain, added to salads, mashed, mixed into soups, or served as a side dish. They are often drizzled with vegetable oil or butter for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool boiled potatoes to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days. Over time the texture and smell may change.
